titulo: Rules and Routes: My Life and My Adventures
titulo_es: Reglas y rutas: mi vida y mis aventuras
estandares: Expreso obligación, prohibición y consejo en contextos cotidianos. Comprendo y doy instrucciones sobre rutinas, normas y desplazamientos.
competencias: Expresar obligación con have to y modales; hablar de cantidades con cuantificadores; usar gerundios después de ciertos verbos y preposiciones; describir tareas del hogar y medios de transporte.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En grupos, los estudiantes diseñan la guía de un viaje escolar: reglas del grupo (have to / mustn't), qué llevar (cuantificadores) y el itinerario con medios de transporte.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In groups, students design the guide for a school trip: group rules (have to / mustn't), what to bring (quantifiers) and the itinerary with means of transport.

lecciones.content_es:
Obligación que viene de fuera

have to expresa una obligación impuesta por una regla o una circunstancia: I have to wear a uniform.

  • Tercera persona: has to — He has to study.
  • Pasado: had to — We had to leave early.

El negativo cambia el significado

  • don't have to = no es necesario (pero puedes): You don't have to come.
  • mustn't = está prohibido: You mustn't smoke here.

Preguntas

Se usan con do/does/did: Do you have to work on Saturdays?
lecciones.content_en:
Obligation that comes from outside

have to expresses an obligation imposed by a rule or a circumstance: I have to wear a uniform.

  • Third person: has to — He has to study.
  • Past: had to — We had to leave early.

The negative changes the meaning

  • don't have to = it is not necessary (but you may): You don't have to come.
  • mustn't = it is forbidden: You mustn't smoke here.

Questions

They use do/does/did: Do you have to work on Saturdays?

lecciones.t: Verbos modales: must, should, can, may
lecciones.t_en: Modal verbs: must, should, can, may
lecciones.content_es:
Qué tienen en común

No cambian nunca (sin -s), van seguidos del verbo en base sin to y forman negativo y pregunta por sí mismos, sin do.

Qué expresa cada uno

  • must – obligación fuerte o deducción: You must study. / He must be tired.
  • should – consejo: You should sleep more.
  • can – habilidad y permiso: I can swim. / Can I go out?
  • may – permiso formal y posibilidad: May I come in? / It may rain.
  • could – posibilidad o petición educada: Could you help me?

Negativos

mustn't (prohibido), shouldn't (no conviene), can't (no puede), may not.
lecciones.content_en:
What they share

They never change (no -s), they are followed by the base verb without to, and they form negatives and questions by themselves, with no do.

What each one expresses

  • must – strong obligation or deduction: You must study. / He must be tired.
  • should – advice: You should sleep more.
  • can – ability and permission: I can swim. / Can I go out?
  • may – formal permission and possibility: May I come in? / It may rain.
  • could – possibility or polite request: Could you help me?

Negatives

mustn't (forbidden), shouldn't (not advisable), can't, may not.

lecciones.content_es:
Dependen de si se puede contar

  • Contables: many, a few, few — many books, a few friends
  • Incontables: much, a little, little — much water, a little sugar
  • Para ambos: a lot of, lots of, some, any, enough, no

La diferencia sutil

  • a few / a little = algunos, un poco (suficiente, positivo)
  • few / little = pocos, poco (casi nada, negativo)

I have a few friends (tengo algunos) vs. I have few friends (tengo muy pocos).

Uso frecuente

much y many aparecen sobre todo en negativos y preguntas; en afirmativo se prefiere a lot of.
lecciones.content_en:
They depend on countability

  • Countable: many, a few, few — many books, a few friends
  • Uncountable: much, a little, little — much water, a little sugar
  • For both: a lot of, lots of, some, any, enough, no

The subtle difference

  • a few / a little = some, a bit (enough, positive)
  • few / little = hardly any (negative)

I have a few friends vs. I have few friends.

Frequent use

much and many appear mostly in negatives and questions; in affirmatives we prefer a lot of.

lecciones.content_es:
El verbo que actúa como sustantivo

Es la forma -ing usada como nombre: Swimming is good for you.

Cuándo se usa

  • Como sujeto de la oración: Reading helps you learn.
  • Después de preposiciones: I'm good at drawing. / Thanks for coming.
  • Después de ciertos verbos: like, love, enjoy, hate, finish, practice, avoid, mind, keep — She enjoys dancing.

Frente al infinitivo

Otros verbos piden to + verbo: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn — I want to travel.

Y unos pocos aceptan los dos sin cambiar el sentido: I like swimming / I like to swim.
lecciones.content_en:
The verb acting as a noun

It is the -ing form used as a noun: Swimming is good for you.

When to use it

  • As the subject: Reading helps you learn.
  • After prepositions: I'm good at drawing. / Thanks for coming.
  • After certain verbs: like, love, enjoy, hate, finish, practice, avoid, mind, keep — She enjoys dancing.

Versus the infinitive

Other verbs take to + verb: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn — I want to travel.

And a few accept both with no change of meaning: I like swimming / I like to swim.

lecciones.content_es:
Números grandes

100 → one hundred · 1.000 → one thousand · 1.000.000 → one million.
Se usa and antes de las decenas finales en inglés británico: 350 = three hundred and fifty.

hundred, thousand y million no llevan -s cuando van con un número: two hundred people, no two hundreds.

Precios

How much is it? — It's twenty dollars. / It costs 15,000 pesos.

Decimales y porcentajes

El punto decimal se lee point: 3.5 = three point five. Los porcentajes: 50% = fifty percent.

Distancias

It's five kilometers from here. The trip takes two hours.
lecciones.content_en:
Large numbers

100 → one hundred · 1,000 → one thousand · 1,000,000 → one million.
British English uses and before the final tens: 350 = three hundred and fifty.

hundred, thousand and million take no -s after a number: two hundred people, not two hundreds.

Prices

How much is it? — It's twenty dollars. / It costs 15,000 pesos.

Decimals and percentages

The decimal point is read point: 3.5 = three point five. Percentages: 50% = fifty percent.

Distances

It's five kilometers from here. The trip takes two hours.

lecciones.content_es:
Las tareas

make the bed (tender la cama), wash the dishes / do the dishes, do the laundry (lavar la ropa), sweep the floor (barrer), mop the floor (trapear), vacuum (aspirar), take out the trash (sacar la basura), set the table (poner la mesa), water the plants, walk the dog, tidy up / clean my room.

Los verbos que se usan

  • do: the dishes, the laundry, the housework, the shopping
  • make: the bed, breakfast, a mess

Con obligación

I have to take out the trash every night. · My brother doesn't have to cook.
lecciones.content_en:
The chores

make the bed, wash the dishes / do the dishes, do the laundry, sweep the floor, mop the floor, vacuum, take out the trash, set the table, water the plants, walk the dog, tidy up / clean my room.

The verbs used

  • do: the dishes, the laundry, the housework, the shopping
  • make: the bed, breakfast, a mess

With obligation

I have to take out the trash every night. · My brother doesn't have to cook.

lecciones.content_es:
Medios de transporte

bus, car, taxi, train, subway / metro, plane, boat, ship, bicycle / bike, motorcycle, on foot (a pie).

La preposición correcta

  • by + medio, sin artículo: by bus, by car, by plane
  • Excepción: on foot
  • Con artículo se usa in o on: in the car, on the bus

Vocabulario de viaje

ticket, luggage (equipaje), suitcase (maleta), passport, airport, flight, trip, journey, tour, book a ticket (reservar).

Frases útiles

How do you get to school? — I go by bus. · The flight takes two hours.
lecciones.content_en:
Means of transport

bus, car, taxi, train, subway / metro, plane, boat, ship, bicycle / bike, motorcycle, on foot.

The right preposition

  • by + means, with no article: by bus, by car, by plane
  • Exception: on foot
  • With an article we use in or on: in the car, on the bus

Travel vocabulary

ticket, luggage, suitcase, passport, airport, flight, trip, journey, tour, book a ticket.

Useful phrases

How do you get to school? — I go by bus. · The flight takes two hours.

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

El periodo trata de reglas y cantidades. Los modales y have to expresan obligación, consejo y permiso; los cuantificadores dicen cuánto hay; y los gerundios aparecen después de preposiciones y de ciertos verbos.

Puntos gramaticales

  • have to = obligación externa · don't have to = no es necesario · mustn't = prohibido.
  • Los modales no cambian, no llevan to y forman preguntas sin do.
  • many/few con contables; much/little con incontables; a lot of para ambos.
  • Gerundio después de preposición y de enjoy, finish, avoid, practice.

Vocabulario

Números grandes, precios y porcentajes; tareas del hogar con do y make; transporte con by y vocabulario de viaje.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The term is about rules and quantities. Modals and have to express obligation, advice and permission; quantifiers say how much there is; and gerunds appear after prepositions and certain verbs.

Grammar points

  • have to = external obligation · don't have to = not necessary · mustn't = forbidden.
  • Modals never change, take no to and form questions without do.
  • many/few with countables; much/little with uncountables; a lot of for both.
  • Gerund after prepositions and after enjoy, finish, avoid, practice.

Vocabulary

Large numbers, prices and percentages; housework with do and make; transport with by and travel vocabulary.
